synthesis: Recent verified developments continue to show the two largest U.S. laboratory competitors combining strong core testing demand with portfolio expansion, but the latest detail sharpens the contrast between their growth profiles. Labcorp reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.731 billion, up 5.8%, with adjusted EPS up 14.9% to $4.99. Acquisitions net of divestitures contributed 1.2 percentage points to consolidated revenue growth and 1.9 points in Diagnostics Laboratories, while the company invested $225.7 million in acquisitions during the quarter. Reported operating margin improved 90 basis points to 12.1%, and adjusted margin rose 70 basis points to 15.8%. Biopharma Laboratory Services was a relative strength, with revenue up 6.5% to $836.2 million and Central Labs up 9.8%. Labcorp raised 2026 revenue-growth and adjusted EPS guidance and expanded its repurchase authorization by $1 billion to $1.4 billion remaining. At the same time, Reuters noted softer-than-expected Diagnostics organic growth versus the benchmark set by Quest, contributing to a negative premarket share reaction despite the earnings beat. Quest’s already verified second-quarter performance remains stronger on top-line momentum: revenue rose 10.2% to $3.043 billion, organic growth was 10.0%, testing volume increased 13.1% and adjusted EPS rose 19.1% to $3.12, followed by higher full-year guidance. Quest continues to expand through consumer and wearable channels, advanced diagnostics and oncology workflow integration, while Labcorp is using acquisitions, specialty testing, laboratory-management agreements, consumer genetics and therapy-linked diagnostics to broaden its growth base. The current competitive pattern favors companies that can combine laboratory scale with differentiated diagnostics, embedded customer channels and operating leverage rather than relying on routine volume alone.

companies.Labcorp: Labcorp’s second quarter showed a balanced mix of organic growth, acquisitions and margin improvement. Revenue increased 5.8% to $3.731 billion; acquisitions net of divestitures added 1.2 percentage points to consolidated growth, and the company deployed $225.7 million on acquisitions. Reported operating margin reached 12.1%, up 90 basis points, while adjusted margin reached 15.8%. Diagnostics revenue grew 5.5% to $2.901 billion, and Biopharma Laboratory Services grew 6.5% to $836.2 million. Labcorp raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $18.10–$18.55 and enterprise revenue-growth guidance to 5.4%–6.3%, while increasing remaining share-repurchase authorization to $1.4 billion. Recent portfolio expansion also includes PTEN companion-diagnostic testing, ColoSense, DPYD genotyping and Marker by Labcorp.
companies.Quest Diagnostics: Quest remains the faster-growing national laboratory in the most recent verified operating comparison. Second-quarter revenue increased 10.2% to $3.043 billion, organic revenue rose 10.0%, testing volume increased 13.1% and adjusted EPS grew 19.1% to $3.12. Quest raised 2026 revenue guidance to $11.95–$12.05 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $11.05–$11.25. Its growth strategy is extending beyond traditional physician and hospital channels through questhealth.com and partnerships with Hims & Hers, Function Health, Whoop and Oura, while advanced diagnostics continue to expand through AD-Detect Alzheimer’s testing, Haystack MRD and oncology workflow integration. Dominique Chokshi’s appointment as Head of Investor Relations adds dedicated shareholder-communications leadership during this period of accelerated growth.

categories.Financials: Labcorp and Quest both raised 2026 outlooks after strong second quarters. Labcorp’s revenue grew 5.8% and adjusted EPS 14.9%, with reported operating margin improving to 12.1%; Quest’s revenue grew 10.2%, organic revenue 10.0% and adjusted EPS 19.1%. Labcorp’s Biopharma segment outperformed consensus expectations, while its Diagnostics organic growth drew greater investor scrutiny relative to Quest’s stronger volume and organic-growth performance.
categories.Product & Services: Labcorp continues to broaden its higher-value menu through PTEN companion-diagnostic testing, ColoSense colorectal screening, DPYD genotyping and Marker by Labcorp consumer genetics. Quest is expanding consumer access and advanced diagnostics through direct-to-consumer and wearable partnerships, Alzheimer’s testing, MRD and oncology workflow integration.
categories.Clinical, R&D: Verified recent clinical evidence supports continued movement toward therapy-linked and molecular diagnostics. Labcorp’s PTEN IHC offering connects an FDA-authorized biomarker test to treatment selection in prostate cancer, while Quest-linked women’s-health evidence supports targeted molecular testing for overlapping vaginitis and STI presentations.
categories.Partnerships & M&A: Labcorp invested $225.7 million in acquisitions during the second quarter; acquisitions net of divestitures contributed 1.2 percentage points to consolidated revenue growth and 1.9 points to Diagnostics Laboratories growth. Quest’s recent expansion is more visible through hospital collaborations, consumer-health platforms and embedded oncology workflows, complementing its acquisition strategy.
categories.Leadership & Organization: Quest appointed Dominique Chokshi as Head of Investor Relations in July 2026. No new verified leadership change from the latest processed Labcorp items altered the existing management picture; Labcorp’s current emphasis is on operating execution, capital allocation and integration of acquired growth.
